newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Insurer in profit,integration on track.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Insurer in profit,integration on track.

text.p: Newly-merged British composite insurer Royal & Sun Alliance (RSA) on Thursday reported a half-year profit that was ahead of market expectations and said it was on target to achieve full integration by 1998.
It confirmed that it expected to see a reduction of 175 million pounds ($274 million) in annual costs by then.
The merger of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance, announced in May, created Britain's biggest insurer with a market capitalisation of 5.4 billion pounds.

Reporting pro-forma interim pre-tax operating profits of 450 million pounds, down from 514 million last year but ahead of most analysts' expectations, the group blamed the slide in profits on a 94 million pound increase in worldwide weather losses.
Total long-term business, meanwhile, rose by 12 percent. The company added that merger expenses amounted to 16 million pounds and related to legal and advisers' costs.
Shares in RSA edged half a penny higher to 412 pence after earlier touching a session high of 420.
"These figures are significantly better than expectations," said ABN Amro Hoare Govett analyst Nick Bunker. "The U.K. commercial lines account has been much better than I thought."

Executive deputy chairman Roger Taylor said Royal & Sun had made rapid progress in integrating the two groups, commenting: "We shall be in a strong position to fulfil our potential as a leading insurance company in the U.K. and internationally."
Group chief executive Richard Gamble said the merger would result in more widely-spread profit sources, with the group less dependent on any one area of the world or any one product line.
He told Reuters that the general business in Britain would contribute 110 million pounds to the previously announced 175 million annual cost savings the group expects to see by 1998.

"There will obviously be major savings on accommodation. There will be a reduction in marketing costs. IT (information technology) development, of course, will be a big item, where both companies are at the moment developing IT systems."
RSA said in May that it would cut 5,000 jobs worldwide, with the U.K. accounting for around 80 percent of this.

At the end of July, the group said it would close 94 branch offices with the loss of around 300 jobs. About 1,000 jobs will go at offices in Liverpool, northern England, and Horsham, southwest of London.
Gamble said it was the group's current intention to move its three telephone-marketed personal lines businesses much closer together over the course of nest year.
The merged company has three such brands -- The Insurance Service, Royal Insurance Direct and Sun Alliance Connections -- which together have two million household and motor policies.
The cost to RSA of restructuring will be equivalent to about one year's savings and details of this are expected at the year-end.

Gamble said that rates were creeping up in the British private motor insurance sector, a highly competitive market which is often seen as an indicator of wider future trends. But he added the gains were very small -- single-digit percentile increases.
The group said it sustained 12 million pounds in losses arising from bombs in Manchester and London's Docklands area. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7721
